stories.title: Clarifying the CATL Tener Sodium, with new specifications and availability
stories.description: New specs for CATL’s four-hour sodium-ion battery reveal how the company will market the product for cost benefits over LFP-based batteries. International deliveries are due to begin in summer 2027.

stories.title: Shinsung E&G unveils 650 W bifacial TOPCon solar modules with 23.25% efficiency
stories.description: South Korean solar manufacturer Shinsung E&G has introduced new n-type TOPCon solar modules for ground-mounted, floating PV and agrivoltaic applications. The bifacial panels feature power outputs ranging from 640 W to 650 W and maximum conversion efficiencies of 23.25%.

stories.title: Scientists find a simple daily routine linked to less pain and depression
stories.description: A simple change to your daily routine could make a surprising difference in how you feel, both physically and mentally. University of Missouri researchers found that older adults who followed consistent daily schedules reported less physical pain and fewer symptoms of depression, even when they struggled with insomnia.

stories.title: Stanford scientists discover hidden brain signals that predict Alzheimer’s years before symptoms
stories.description: Stanford researchers have discovered that hidden patterns of brain activity can predict Alzheimer’s risk years before memory problems appear, potentially offering an earlier warning than traditional biomarkers. The same patterns also reveal which brains are unusually resistant to aging, raising hopes for future treatments that could help protect memory.

stories.title: Scientists discover a bizarre paradox among endangered penguins
stories.description: A groundbreaking drone survey has revealed a startling split in the fate of New Zealand's endangered Erect-crested penguins. While one population has remained stable for decades, another has declined by more than 40%, apparently due to a combination of predators, worsening storms, and changing ocean conditions.

stories.title: First attempt to address screen printing-induced degradation in copper-plated heterojunction solar cells
stories.description: Researchers in China have investigated a previously overlooked degradation mechanism in copper-plated heterojunction solar cells caused by screen-printed photoresist. They found that progressive wear of the screen mesh can damage the cells' passivation layers and reduce efficiency.
